inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL UPDATE IGNORE migration changes selected legacy codes while allowing conflicting rows to remain unchanged instead of aborting the statement.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored spell-alias cleanup. UPDATE IGNORE attempts to canonicalize two legacy codes under a unique constraint; one row conflicts with an existing canonical code and remains unchanged, while the other moves to a free replacement code. The source table, values, labels, and game semantics are not copied.

fixture_notes: Alias 1 targets an already-occupied canonical code and must remain unchanged; alias 2 targets an unused replacement code and must update. The unique constraint makes UPDATE IGNORE behavior observable.
determinism_notes: Alias IDs and replacement codes are fixed, and final rows are ordered by the primary key; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE spell_aliases (alias_id INT PRIMARY KEY, spell_code INT NOT NULL UNIQUE, spell_name VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL, active TINYINT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE IGNORE spell_aliases SET spell_code = CASE WHEN alias_id = 1 THEN 7386 ELSE 8390 END WHERE spell_code IN (7405, 8380)

checks.sql: SELECT alias_id, spell_code, spell_name, active FROM spell_aliases ORDER BY alias_id
SELECT spell_code, COUNT(*) AS code_count FROM spell_aliases GROUP BY spell_code ORDER BY spell_code
